scope.description: Which product this test is authored for — the target key, e.g. `automation-exercise`. In chat the planner fills this from the person's own words: a request that names the page, product or site it is for supplies the scope, and nothing needs to be typed. Calling `/fn authoring.draft.write` directly, pass it explicitly — `{"scope":{"tier":"product","key":"<target>"}}` — whenever this project scaffolds more than one target. When it is omitted the host derives it ONLY where the project has exactly one candidate product; otherwise the call returns a typed refusal that names every candidate so you can choose one. It never guesses at a product, because authoring against a guessed product writes a test for the wrong application.

window.description: Which drafts to count — a span of history, NOT a product. `{"scope":"session","sessionRef":"<id>"}` counts only what this conversation authored; `{"scope":"all-time"}` counts every draft this workspace has evaluated; `{"scope":"last-n","n":<count>}` counts the N most recently evaluated, newest first. In chat you never type this: the session supplies its own window, and asking about the current conversation is the default. Do not confuse it with `authoring.draft.write`'s `scope`, which names the product a test is authored for.
